title: Edge proxy IP misattribution causing tenant-quota mischarging and silent-retry amplification
creator: Samira Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-17 between 15:42 and 16:30 UTC a subset of tenants experienced elevated 429s and unexpected quota consumption spikes. Root cause: the edge proxy (v1.12) started normalizing X-Forwarded-For headers from a newly onboarded CDN peering partner; in certain request shapes the proxy replaced the actual client IP with the last hop IP. This caused per-tenant quota keys (which are partially keyed by client IP for burst isolation) to be attributed to the wrong tenant bucket. Compounding the problem, some SDK clients silently retried on 429s without propagating Retry-After; retries were proxied with the same misattributed IP causing rapid amplification and tenant-level throttles. Impact: a handful of high-throughput tenants saw sudden quota exhaustion, degraded throughput and billing anomalies. Internal dashboards flagged a 12x increase in bucket collision events and a 4x rise in 429 rate for impacted regions.
timeline: 2026-02-17 15:40 UTC - First alert from synthetic canaries in us-east-1. 2026-02-17 15:48 UTC - Support tickets from two customers reporting sudden throttling. 2026-02-17 16:05 UTC - On-call identified spike in 'quota_key_collisions' metric. 2026-02-17 16:20 UTC - Hotfix: rollback edge-proxy v1.12 to v1.11 in affected POPs. 2026-02-17 17:15 UTC - Throttles dropped to baseline; tickets updated. 2026-02-18 - Full root cause analysis started; formed cross-functional task force.
root_cause: Edge proxy header normalization logic (introduced to mitigate forged XFF) incorrectly used the last recorded hop for IPv6-mapped and proxied TCP connections behind the new CDN peering. Quota key composition logic assumed client IP stability; when IP was overwritten, multiple tenants sharing the same burst policy collided into the same quota bucket. Silent SDK retries without honoring Retry-After amplified the load into the wrong bucket. Unit tests did not cover the CDN peering header shapes and the integration contract for Retry-After propagation was underspecified.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Rolled back edge-proxy v1.12 to v1.11 in affected POPs (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/5123). 2) Emergency patch to add a strict prefer-client-ip flag for known CDN peers and to log XFF anomalies (hotfix branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/compare/hotfix/xff-guard). 3) Applied rate-limiter circuit to reject silent retries after 2 attempts where Retry-After absent (gateway config temporary rule id gf-2026-02-17).
long_term_action_items: 1) Update quota key design to avoid client-IP as a sole shard key for tenant burst isolation; add tenant-scoped hashed nonce (owner: @Diego Martinez; due 2026-03-18). 2) Harden edge-proxy XFF handling: explicit trusted-proxy ACL + canonicalization tests for CDN peering shapes (owner: @Lina Zhao; due 2026-03-08). 3) SDKs: require honoring and surface Retry-After to application layer; add integration test that simulates 429 + client retry behavior (owner: @Miguel Torres; due 2026-03-22). 4) Observability: add 'quota_key_collision' alert with automated anomalous-tenant-sampling and an on-call playbook (owner: @Samira Patel; due 2026-03-01). 5) Deploy a canary for new proxy behavior with traffic shadowing and deterministic XFF mutation checks (owner: infra; due 2026-04-01).
tests_and_validation_plan: - Add unit + integration tests for X-Forwarded-For normalization covering: multiple proxies, IPv6-mapped, and CDN peering header ordering. - Synthetic replay harness: replay captured edge traces through proxy testbed and assert quota_key stability. - SDK conformance tests: ensure Retry-After propagation and exponential backoff adhered. - Post-deploy: 48-hour elevated monitoring window with automated rollback threshold (429 rate > 3x baseline for 10 minutes).

resolution_summary: Hotfix rollback restored baseline traffic levels; deploys include XFF anomaly logging and a temporary prefer-client-ip flag. Long-term fixes target quota key redesign, stronger proxy ACL/canonicalization, and SDK retry conformance. Customer notifications are prepared and billing reconciliation for mischarged quota buckets is in progress.
postmortem_notes: Lessons learned: never assume header shapes remain stable when onboarding new transit providers; quota sharding should avoid single external attributes that can be rewritten by intermediaries. Investment in end-to-end synthetic replay tests for new peering partners will pay off. Consider a policy that clients must surface Retry-After to the app layer to avoid silent amplification.
